reason: Conversation 1 reached the correct diagnosis and gave Neff-specific, step-by-step clock-setting instructions (clock button or +/- together, flashing 'A' manual mode, confirm) that resolved the fault, with sensible fallbacks and no unsupported part or engineer claims. Conversation 2 identified the right cause early, but its opener was a wall of US-flavoured generic possibilities, it never asked for the make, and when the homeowner asked which button to press it repeated the same vague paragraph nearly verbatim, including an odd and unhelpful aside that '0.00' is 'not a standard error code for this brand'. Neither raised safety concerns inappropriately, but 1 was more efficient, more accurate and actually got the oven working.
